frames.frame: [统计/陈述], compared with [对比数据/群体]（句尾后置对照）
frames.gloss: 先给一组数字或断言，再后置 compared with 引出对照组数据，形成'甲 vs 乙'的统计对照
frames.notes: 已登记的是句首版 'Compared to/with [A], [主句]'；本变体把 compared with 挂在句尾，学习者常把它误析为主句谓语的一部分（尤其前面 say/are 已出现限定动词时），需识别它是无动词的补充状语。本批出现 5 次（0498/0500/0503/0509/0343）

examples.text: 71% of parents with a college degree say they do it every day, compared with 33% of those with a high school diploma or less.
Discipline techniques vary by education level: 8% of those with a postgraduate degree say they often beat their children, compared with 22% of those with a high school degree or less.
While bullying is parents' greatest concern over all, nearly half of low-income parents worry their child will get shot, compared with one-fifth of high-income parents.

frames.related: Compared to/with [A] / Unlike [A], [主句]（已登记句首版；此为句尾后置统计对照新变体）

frames.frame: Of [限定群体], [X%/those who] [V]（of 前置分母）
frames.gloss: 句首 Of 短语先限定'分母'人群，逗号后主句给出该人群中的百分比或 those who 子集的行为
frames.notes: 分母被前移到句首，主句主语只剩百分比或 those 指代；学习者易把 Of 短语误当作后面动词的宾语或漏掉它对百分比的限定范围。本批出现 4 次（0319/0495/0496/0505，其中 0505 百分比数字被 OCR 吞掉但仍可辨骨架）

examples.text: Of the 300 employees participating in the study, those who experienced high levels of telepressure were more likely to agree with statements assessing burnout, like “I’ve no energy for going to work in the morning,” and to report feeling fatigued and unfocused.

Of families earning more than $75,000 a year, 84% say their children have participated in organized sports over the past year, 64% have done volunteer work and 62% have taken lessons in music, dance or art.
Of families earning less than $30,000, 59% of children have done sports, 37% have volunteered and 41% have taken arts classes.

frames.frame: [A] failure to [V], (插入语), [谓语 + 宾语]（名词化主语）
frames.gloss: failure to do 整体名词化作主语，谓语（indicates/exposes 等）在其后，中间可再插入 however 或长修饰
frames.notes: 名词化 failure to + 动词原形占据主语位，真正谓语被推后；0388 中 however 插在主谓之间、且 to 的宾语被副词隔开（address comprehensively the problem），是典型读慢点：学习者易把 failure/expose 错配为主谓。本批 2 次（0322/0388）

examples.text: And because a failure to accept these increased demands indicates a lack of commitment to one’s work, the employee complies. [K] To address skyrocketing employee stress levels, many companies have implemented workplace wellness programs, partnering with health care providers that have created programs to promote employee health and well- being.
Failure to address compre hensively the problem of greenhouse gas emissions, however, exposes all generations, present and future, to incalcul able risks.

frames.frame: [A of X] … than/other than that of [B]（that 回指对照）
frames.gloss: that of B 回指前文同类名词，形成'A 的标准/款式'与'B 的'之间的对照
frames.notes: that 指代上位名词（standard/sportswear），再接 of 短语；other than that of pure beauty 中双重虚词叠加（other than + that of），回指链需要回跳到主语名词，是真实读慢点。本批 2 次（0445/0452）

examples.text: Designer sportswear was not modeled on that of Europe, as “modem art” would later be; it was genuinely invented and developed in America.
Designer sportswear would have to be verified by a standard other than that of pure beauty; the emulation of a designer’s life in designer sportswear was a crude version of this relationship.

frames.related: [A组] than those who did(n't)（对照回指）——同一'替代词回指对照'家族，that of 回指物、those who 回指人

frames.frame: [S] find oneself / find yourself [V-ing/补语]（不自觉进入状态）
frames.gloss: find oneself + 状态补语：不知不觉发现自己处于某状态，而非主动'寻找'
frames.notes: 反身代词 + 补语结构，学习者易按字面读成'发现自己'的主动搜寻义；实际语义是'（不知不觉）处于/变成'，后可接 V-ing（using）或形容词（distracted）。本批 2 次（0570/0573）

examples.text: The technology, your boss, and your friends, all influence how often you find yourself using (or overusing )these gadgets.
Like Schwartz and so many others, I often find myself distracted and off tack.

frames.frame: [X]—[插入语]—[续写]（双破折号插入打断）
frames.gloss: 双破折号把插入语（同位语、if any、来源评注）塞进句子中间，被隔开的前后两段必须跨过插入语接续成句
frames.notes: 标点对骨架：插入语可打在主谓之间（0407 sharers—…—get noticed）、并列名词与 and 之间（0514 households—…—and）或 wh-词与名词之间（0354 which—if any—battery technology）。读慢点在恢复被隔断的主谓/修饰线；本批 3 次（0354/0407/0514），另有尾随单破折号展开（见 candidates）

examples.text: No one knows which---if any---battery technology will ultimately dominate, but one thing remains clear.
The most successful sharers—those whose data are downloaded and cite d the most often---get noticed, and their work gets used.

More than a quarter of children live in single-parent households—a historic high, according to Pew—and these children are three times as likely to live in poverty as those who live with married parents.
